chunks: Is'haq said: 'Umar ibn Abī Muslim narrated to me, saying:

A man from the people of Egypt, called Sayf ibn al-Layth, came to us in Surr Man Ra'a, complaining to al-Muhtadī about an estate of his which Shafīʿ al-Khādim had usurped from him and from which he had expelled him. So we advised him to write to Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام and ask him to facilitate its affair.

So Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام wrote to him: 'There is no harm upon you. Your estate will be returned to you, so do not go forward to the ruler. Meet the agent in whose hand the estate is, and frighten him with the Greatest Sovereign, Allah, Lord of the worlds.'

So he met him, and the agent in whose hand the estate was said to him: 'It had been written to me at the time of your departure from Egypt that I should seek you out and return the estate to you.' So he returned it to him by the judgment of the judge Ibn Abī al-Shawārib and the testimony of the witnesses, and he had no need to proceed to al-Muhtadī. Thus the estate became his and remained in his possession, and there was no further issue concerning it after that.

He said: And this Sayf ibn al-Layth narrated to me, saying: 'I left behind in Egypt, when I departed from it, a son of mine who was ill, and another son of mine older than him who was my trustee and caretaker over my dependants and my estates. So I wrote to Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام asking him to supplicate for my sick son.'

So he wrote to me: 'Your afflicted son has recovered, and the elder one—your trustee and caretaker—has died. So praise Allah and do not grieve in a way that would nullify your reward.' Then the news reached me that my son had indeed recovered from his illness, and that the elder one died on the day the reply of Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام reached me.

key_terms.الدُّعَاءَ: supplication requested from the Imam for the sick son
key_terms.السُّلْطَانِ الْأَعْظَمِ: the Greatest Sovereign, meaning Allah, invoked as the supreme authority
key_terms.الْمُهْتَدِي: the ruling caliph to whom the complaint was intended to be taken
key_terms.الْوَكِيلُ: the agent in possession of and handling the estate
key_terms.ضَيْعَةٌ: an estate or landed property belonging to a person
key_terms.فَاحْمَدِ اللَّهَ: give praise to Allah in response to what has occurred
key_terms.قَيِّمِي: my caretaker or manager over dependants and property
key_terms.وَصِيِّي: my trustee or executor entrusted with affairs after me

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the guidance and knowledge of Imam al-Hasan al-Askari عليه السلام in resolving disputes and informing believers about unseen events?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates two incidents connected to Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام: the restoration of Sayf ibn al-Layth’s usurped estate and the Imam’s report concerning the recovery of one son and the death of another. It highlights the Imam’s guidance in worldly matters, reliance upon Allah, and foreknowledge manifested in events that occurred as he stated.
